author: ojiudezue
title: Optimization Coordinator pivots to an agent-first, risk-tiered self-fixing house
summary: The OC will become a URA-specialized reasoning agent (HA + URA + config + operator doctrine + goals, with a tiered tool catalogue) that runs nightly, diagnoses with retrieved evidence, acts alone within risk tiers and verifies its fixes, instead of more static detector code.
why: Static per-signal detectors produced ~90% noise (5,305 findings / 72 real problems in 14 d; 0 scored samples), while the manual context-reason-fix-verify loop diagnosed several real faults in one session (solar counter flap, missing exit rows, Foyer BLE pull). Operator: 'the main unlock should be context, reasoning, goals and loops'; 'we just need a risk level taxonomy where it can act alone'. A unified coordinator request API was rejected on cost/benefit (~6 Tier-3 cycles vs ~2 using existing coordinator paths).
implications: Tiers: R0 observe (always), R1 silent reversible fixes like integration reload/fan recheck/unstick sensor (alone overnight, verified, auto-demoted), R2 occupant-visible (only promoted fix types, never while asleep), R3 never alone (HA restart, battery/EV, locks, deletes, money). The only static trust machinery is an action log driving promotion/demotion. Runs outside HA first. Goals ranked from a canned list; room memory is evidence; R2 actions use each coordinator's existing in-process paths (optimization.py HVAC bypass removed).
revisit_trigger: End of the ~2-week R0 judging period: if the agent's diagnoses are not mostly right, stop before granting R1.
